read: Whole supplied transcript, 00:03 Medi through 1:03:21 Amal, in order.
coverage_note: Counted 358 Arabic-bearing Medi turns, including fragments, recognizable Latin transliteration, and Arabic quoted inside English discussion. Long English-only explanations, pauses, and background conversations were read but not treated as Arabic errors. No auxiliary echo-candidates or confusables file was supplied. Echo readings: hawaii = أواعي; kani ishi / ishi kani = تاني إشي / إشي تاني; Allah akhir il tariq = على آخر الطريق; yipsut refers to يبسط. Amal's 'Be upset' is an engine rendering of بيبسط. Speech is missing around 35:37–36:48; the determiner row there relies on Amal explicitly quoting his form. Excluded his self-fixes of بصوت, خططت, واحدة, حلو, and طريق; excluded questions about هو/هي, demonstrative + واحد, and الإشي التاني. Did not turn the green-food/dish clarification or the suggestion to move كمان in the fiancée sentence into extra slips. The final بيبسط drill contains root-letter/order pronunciation problems explicitly identified by Amal as pronunciation; these were not counted as vocabulary or grammar errors. Clothing transcription and chat disagree about colors, so no additional color-agreement row was forced. The spoken year differs from the lesson date, but there is no voiced language correction of it. Uncertain form retrieval at 13:52 and the noisy idafa exchange at 32:58 are retained at low confidence.

rows.medi_said: أنا رحت، أمم، على مطعم مع صحابي والـ مطعم صوت عالي كتير
rows.why: Best reading is that the restaurant's sound was loud, requiring صوته after المطعم, although a construction with فيه صوت would also express his meaning.
rows.english: I went to a restaurant with my friends, and it was very loud.

rows.chat: ana mit7ammes la-bukra 3ashaan bukra m5a66et ishi
rows.why: She echoes the English preposition and prompts him to replace it with لَ, eliciting متحمّس لبكرا; the sheet row is 'for / to | la | لَ | la'.
rows.english: I am excited for tomorrow because...

rows.amal_said: Oh, we would say خميس الجاي cause it's next Thursday. We're still in this week.
rows.why: He means the Thursday still to come, and she explicitly corrects how to identify that day with الجاي.
rows.english: I am going this coming Thursday.

rows.medi_said: اليوم بلبس بلوزة نص كم. white
rows.chat: el-yoam balbes bluze noss kum soda u bantaloan azra2 u kundara soda
rows.why: The English color completes his Arabic clothing description without a voiced Arabic replacement; the sheet row is 'white (m/f) | Abyad | أبيض | abyad', with بيضا the best agreeing form here.
rows.english: Today I am wearing a white short-sleeved shirt.

rows.why: She changes كان to كانت and then explains that the verb refers to feminine مرة.
rows.english: The first time I tried Arabic food was the same time...

rows.chat: awal marra ana jarrabet akel 3arabi kaanat nafs el-marra illi ana elta2ait ma3 emm 5atibti la-awal marra.
rows.why: He rejects her 'Tlat' echo with 'لا، I met' and she supplies Alta'at, suggesting failed verb-form retrieval, although the noisy first attempt could conceal only a pronunciation slip.
rows.english: I met my fiancée.

rows.amal_said: What does alta'at take؟ There is two options.
rows.chat: awal marra ana jarrabet akel 3arabi kaanat nafs el-marra illi ana elta2ait ma3 emm 5atibti la-awal marra.
rows.why: He follows the meeting verb directly with خطيبتي, and her fixed-preposition prompt elicits مع, which she accepts.
rows.english: I met with my fiancée.

rows.chat: awal marra ana jarrabet akel 3arabi kaanat nafs el-marra illi ana elta2ait ma3 emm 5atibti la-awal marra.
rows.why: In a new attempt several minutes after the earlier correction, he again uses masculine كان for مرة and she immediately supplies كانت.
rows.english: It was the same time that I met my fiancée's mother.

rows.amal_said: Mm-mm-mm. How do you say two years؟
rows.why: She rejects the separate number plus plural years and explicitly prompts the dual form until he says سنتين.
rows.english: More than two years ago.

rows.amal_said: I tried. You have to point back to it.
rows.chat: awal akel ana jarrabto kaan 7umus u zaitoon
rows.why: After fronting أول أكل, he omits the object ending, and she explicitly tells him to point back to it.
rows.english: The first food I tried was hummus and olives.

rows.chat: taani akel ana jarrabto msa55an. u kaan fi  aa5er el-3asha 7ilu falastini
rows.why: In the new تاني أكل sentence she stops at أنا after his unsuffixed verb, and only after that cue does he supply جربته.
rows.english: The second food I tried was musakhan.

rows.medi_said: Oh، no، I forgot the name. What is this name? The, the one with the bread and the pomegranate and the chicken?
rows.chat: taani akel ana jarrabto msa55an. u kaan fi  aa5er el-3asha 7ilu falastini
rows.why: He explicitly asks for the dish's name and she supplies مسخن; this is a retrieval gap, not a wrong Arabic ingredient word.
rows.english: What is the dish with bread and chicken called?

rows.chat: taani akel ana jarrabto msa55an. u kaan fi  aa5er el-3asha 7ilu falastini
rows.why: Best reading is that he forgot the name of the singular حلو فلسطيني just mentioned, so the possessive ending should be singular rather than هم.
rows.english: I forgot its name.

rows.medi_said: uh، احنا عندنا مطعم اسم mata مناقيش.
rows.why: The best grammatical reading is مطعم اسمه followed by its name, but the missing ه could also be transcription loss and Amal gives no correction.
rows.english: We have a restaurant called Mata Manaqeesh.

rows.medi_said: Uh، كليًا الـ مفضل uh، أكل-- no. أكل
rows.why: He confirms that he used كليًا to mean 'in general', and she explains that it means 'completely' before supplying بشكل عام.
rows.english: In general, my favorite Palestinian food is...

rows.medi_said: fuck، I don't remember if مفضل goes before or after. أكل المفضل، مفضل الأكل. No، أكل المفضل.
rows.why: After his final choice of أكل المفضل, she twice supplies الأكل so the noun and favorite adjective form the definite phrase he intends.
rows.english: My favorite food.

rows.why: Her 'Every' flags the meaning of his indefinite noun, and he then adds the articles to express all Palestinian food rather than every individual food.
rows.english: All Palestinian food, in general.

rows.chat: bshakel 3aam el-akel el-mufaddal 3indi / akli el-mufaddal ma2loobe u shu esem el-akle el-5adra.
rows.why: In a fresh attempt several minutes later, he again omits the noun's article and she recasts the complete favorite phrase.
rows.english: My favorite food is maqluba.

rows.medi_said: مقلوبة ush. Uh, shu ism el akel,
rows.why: He asks for the name and describes the green dish in the following fragments, and she supplies ملوخية.
rows.english: What is the green dish called?

rows.medi_said: I don't need to put andi, right? Akli il mufaddal khatibti
rows.amal_said: You would have to link خطيبتي. يعني لا خطيبتي or عند خطيبتي. And you'd have to say هذي الأكلة because this is
rows.right: هذي الأكلة المفضلة عند خطيبتي كمان
rows.why: When they return to his original wording, she explicitly rejects it and explains that خطيبتي needs a linking preposition and that the noun must be الأكلة, not his possessive أكلي.
rows.english: This is also my fiancée's favorite dish.

rows.why: While completing أكلة خطيبتي, he says the masculine favorite adjective and she supplies the feminine form agreeing with أكلة.
rows.english: My fiancée's favorite dish.

rows.medi_said: il m- no, no. Uh, il hawaii imi?
rows.why: His repeated article-bearing possession attempts precede her poorly transcribed prompt and his accepted أواعي إمي, suggesting an idafa correction, though the exact voiced instruction is unclear.
rows.english: My mother's clothes.

rows.why: He changes his earlier plural adjective to feminine singular during the prompt, and she explicitly restores the plural favorite form for أواعي.
rows.english: These are my mother's favorite clothes.

rows.amal_said: الطريق التاني. ... No, you said طريق التاني.
rows.why: The engine loses his speech after خلّينا, but Amal explicitly quotes his طريق التاني at 36:30 after supplying the corrected definite noun phrase at 36:26.
rows.english: Let's go by the other route.

rows.amal_said: No, we would just say هذي or هذا. Why do I say هذي؟ هذا.
rows.why: She supplies the Arabic demonstrative for the English chunk completing his Arabic clause; the sheet includes 'this (m) | Hada | هادا | hada' and 'one | Wa7ad | واحد | wa7ad'.
rows.english: Because this one is scary.

rows.amal_said: Mm, this is scared. What's scary?
rows.why: He describes the road as experiencing fear instead of causing it, and her 'It scares' prompt eventually elicits بخوّف after the intermediate مخاف and بخاف attempts.
rows.english: This road is scary.

rows.why: For the intended additional movie she prompts him to swap the words, and he immediately changes film kamaan to kamaan film.
rows.english: Let's watch one more movie.

rows.medi_said: بشرب... Oh, I don't know how to say drink. شرب.
rows.wrong: I don't know how to say drink
rows.why: After he explicitly says he does not know the beverage noun, she supplies عصير as the example noun, so this is supplied vocabulary rather than a scored claim that drink literally means juice.
rows.english: A drink or juice, as the noun for the exercise.

rows.amal_said: Ashan it is ahsan. You could say ashano, ashano or ashan huwa ahsan.
rows.chat: an troo7i 3ala awal taree2. roo7i 3ala taani waa7ad 3ashaanno a7san
rows.proposed_rule: When عشان introduces an adjective clause giving a reason, express its subject with a pronoun or a suffix: عشان هو أحسن / عشانه أحسن, not bare عشان أحسن.
rows.why: After his عشان ... أحسن she explicitly supplies the missing 'it' and gives both the independent-pronoun and suffixed alternatives, which is not merely a copula or pronoun-gender correction.
rows.english: Go by the second route because it is better.

rows.amal_said: Yes. So no preposition needed. 'Cause it makes them happy. أمم.
rows.why: He inserts لَ before the people made happy, and she explicitly explains that causative بيبسط takes them directly without a preposition.
rows.english: Halloween makes little children happy.

rows.medi_said: Uh, for little-- El walad or walad. No. Yeah, el walad. El walad el zahar.
rows.why: His final attempted phrase still uses singular الولد for the requested children, and she supplies the plural الأولاد.
rows.english: Little children.

rows.medi_said: أغلـ أغلب الـ No, it's أغلب إشي
rows.why: He abandons the article and asserts أغلب إشي, but she explicitly says the article is required and elicits aghlab il ishi.
rows.english: Most of the thing or things being discussed.
